deep.reconstruction:
There are no formulas or derivations on this page. It is a short philosophical and didactic preamble to a 'geometry (Raumlehre, struck) of 4 dimensions'.

(1) Riemann announces that he will study a 4-dimensional geometry. He calls it a 'manifold of points' (Mannigfaltigkeit von Punkten) of greater extent than the whole infinite (3-dimensional) space.

(2) He concedes that intuition (Anschauung) cannot grasp at one time a region of points larger than the whole infinite space.

(3) Remedy: we can place ourselves into different spaces at different times. Concretely:
- first imagine the whole infinite 3-space;
- later imagine again the whole infinite 3-space;
- but think that the points now being viewed are all different from those viewed before.

In modern terms (my gloss): R^4 is presented as a one-parameter family of disjoint copies of R^3, i.e. R^4 = union over t of {t} x R^3. The parameter is first motivated as the successive moments of imagining, not as a geometric coordinate.

(4) He draws an epistemological distinction:
- thinking two points as coexisting (gleichzeitig vorhanden) in the 4-manifold;
- picturing them simultaneously (gleichzeitig vorstellen) in intuition.

(5) Criterion: one can simultaneously picture a set of coexisting points only if one knows they all lie in a single (3-dimensional) space. In modern terms: a configuration of points in R^4 is visualizable at once only if it lies in a single 3-dimensional subspace (gloss mine, likely an affine hyperplane or a slice t = const).

The text breaks off here. The roman 'I' under the last line is probably a reference or continuation mark.

Context: the previous folio is an unrelated Hanoverian geodesy memorandum, so the bundle is miscellaneous. The idea matches the 1854 Habilitationsvortrag. There, an (n+1)-fold extended manifold arises when an n-fold manifold passes continuously and determinately into another, and points are located by successive specification. This page reads like an early or popular draft of that constructive and epistemological viewpoint, specialised to n = 3.
errors: No mathematical errors; the page contains no computation.

The criterion 'only if they all lie in one space' is stated loosely: 'Raum' must mean a 3-dimensional subspace (slice or hyperplane) of the 4-manifold. Riemann does not specify whether only the slices t = const or arbitrary 3-flats are meant.

results.what: 4-dimensional point manifold constructed or visualized as a one-parameter family of disjoint whole 3-spaces, traversed successively ('at different times')
results.modern_name: R^4 as R x R^3 / foliation by hyperplanes; 'time-slice' visualization of the fourth dimension
results.usually_credited_to: Higher-dimensional geometry: Grassmann 1844, Cayley 1843/45, Schläfli 1850-52 (published later), Riemann 1854/1868. Popular time-slice visualizations: later 19th c. (e.g. Hinton 1880s).

results.what: Distinction between points coexisting in the manifold and points simultaneously representable in intuition; only points in one 3-space are simultaneously intuitable
results.modern_name: Epistemology of higher-dimensional space (Herbartian Vorstellung vs. existence); limits of spatial intuition
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann's Habilitationsvortrag 1854 (with Herbart's influence); later Helmholtz 1870s

deep.surprise_reason: Riemann's n-dimensional manifolds and the inductive construction of an (n+1)-fold manifold from n-fold ones are well known from the 1854 lecture. This explicitly 4-dimensional, 'time-successive' visualization draft, possibly from 1853, is a nice unpublished illustration of the genesis of those ideas. It contains no new mathematical result.

checkable.asserts: The 4-manifold of points (x,y,z,t) has four independent coordinates, one more than ordinary space; t indexes the successive copies of 3-space (illustrative only).

Illustration of the criterion: points sharing t = 0 (here three points plus the origin) lie in one 3-space, so their span relative to it has dimension at most 3. This is a trivial check of the 'one space' condition, not a theorem from the page.

transcription_corrections: 'Riemann 26' (top left) is a later archival label, not Riemann's text; the pencil '58' in the right margin is the folio number.
Line 1: the struck word after 'einer' is plausibly 'Raumlehre' but is uncertain in the image; the sense survives as 'einer ... von 4 Dimensionen'.

Line 7-8: the struck words appear to be 'nach in' ('aber wir können uns [-nach in-] zu verschiedenen Zeiten in verschiedene Räume versetzen'); the transcription's leftover 'in zu' should be just 'zu'.
Line 9: 'Ich stelle mir zuerst' — the last word is hard to read and may be 'zuerst' or 'jetzt'; sense unaffected.

Line 13-14: the transcription marks 'andere' as deleted, but then the sentence ('sämtlich seien, als die Punkte') makes no sense. Read 'dass die Punkte, die ich jetzt anschaue, sämtlich andere seien, als die Punkte, die ich vorher anschaute': 'sämtlich' is inserted above the line and 'andere' is retained, or the struck word is a variant of it.
The 'I' under 'Raume' on the last line is a separate mark (probably a continuation or reference sign), not part of the text.
